lines.text: Task two was about the billing service. The agent spent the whole job inside invoices.
Task three is about the signup form. A different part of the product, and a different job.
But the agent keeps talking about invoices, as if the last job never ended.
That is context bleed. Leftover assumptions from the last task creep into the new one.
And the mistakes look plausible, so you may not catch them until much later.
You could clear the context by hand between tasks, if you remember every single time.
Agent R Q sends slash clear to a Claude Code agent right before it picks up a task.
The agent reads only the new task, and its own notes saved in workspace memory.
Now the answer matches the job. Signup form, got it, starting.
Lessons that help still carry over, because the notes live in memory, not in the chat.
Clean context means fewer confident mistakes, and fewer surprises in review.
What is the most confidently wrong thing an agent ever told you? Share it below, and try clear context at Agent R Q dot com.
